title: Try the segmented thumb on the system's own Liquid Glass morph
goal: User 2026-09-29, after asking whether Swift gives real Liquid Glass or we fake it: they want the thumb moved by macOS's own glass morph instead of the hand-written per-frame animation. Today (50cda9d8) the thumb is a real .glassEffect capsule, but it is placed frame by frame by a TimelineView running SegmentThumbMorph, with glassEffectID removed; that fixed the overshoot (filmed: 0 frames off the rail) but the motion is still ours, not the system's, and the lighter look is a gradient painted over the glass. Build the system version and compare the two on real frames.
acceptance: The thumb's motion comes from the system: a real .glassEffect capsule behind the selected segment, in a GlassEffectContainer, with one .glassEffectID shared across the segment slots (or matchedGeometryEffect on a single glass capsule, whichever the system morphs natively), the selection changed inside withAnimation with the system's own smooth curve; no TimelineView placement and no SegmentThumbMorph for a click
Only one animator: the pick is isolated from any outer withAnimation (e.g. View/Edit's mode animation) so nothing adds to the morph (the cause found in 50cda9d8)

Lighter than the rail through the glass itself (.tint on the glass, or the clear/regular variant over the recessed rail), no gradient painted over it; measured thumb vs rail contrast at least 1.5:1 in light and dark, title bar and panel
Filmed with the filmThumb walk step at 120 fps, all four moves: no thumb pixel outside the rail, no overshoot past rest
Drag to slide still follows the pointer and lands on release
Behind a temporary flag so both versions can be compared; a card asks the user to try both (with filmed frames side by side) and pick; the loser is deleted after the answer

log.note: User 2026-09-29: they did not reject a Liquid Glass segmented control; they rejected the first version because it looked like two separate buttons with no animation. A stock Picker(.segmented) / NSSegmentedControl rendered as a real single glass control is a fair third candidate to film alongside ours if it can wear the component's look.
User 2026-09-29 17:34: decided. They want the system glass morph, consistently, everywhere. No need for a side-by-side card; the follow-up one-segmented-look task makes it the only style.
